source_terms: A grid's orthogonal (90° axis) logic, and all the thinking about how to work with it, derive from the fundamental verbivisual qualities of type.
Stacking horizontal sentences below each other creates a new vertical line—the column—and columns appearing side by side establish yet another horizontal structure.
item.claim: The right-angled logic of the grid is not imposed mathematics; it grows out of the physical form of type. Letters in the Western alphabet are built from vertical strokes; sequenced into words and sentences those verticals form a horizontal line; sentences stacked form a new vertical, the column; columns set side by side establish a further horizontal structure.

mechanism.text: The alternation between vertical and horizontal at each level of assembly is what produces an orthogonal structure. The source states the chain explicitly, level by level.

caveats.text: the source names the Western alphabet specifically as the basis of the claim
no non-Latin writing system is discussed, so whether the derivation holds for scripts with different stroke logic is not addressed

positive.description: diagram accompanying the claim that the structural approach grows organically from typographic form

intra_source_relations.note: explains why a grid is orthogonal at all

item.visible_content: Four panels in two rows. Left of each row, a poster for the same event — a Hear-Say reading by Henry Magaziner at a Philadelphia bookshop, with the same date, time and address. Right of each row, the alignment structure that composition implies, drawn as teal rules. Top row: the information is set as one flush-right stack, and the derived structure is two fields divided by a single vertical axis. Bottom row: the same information is broken into several differently-weighted groups scattered across the format, and the derived structure is a multi-field grid of roughly five vertical and five horizontal divisions.
item.what_the_visual_supports: That a grid is READ OFF a composition rather than imposed on it. The content is held constant and only the grouping changes, and the structure changes with it. It also supports the source's narrower claim that a large variety of layouts is reachable inside strict limits: both posters use one type family and a small set of sizes.
item.requires_prose: That like information is grouped and disparate information separated, and that changes in weight and scale are what introduce hierarchy. The picture shows the outcome; the caption supplies the rule that produced it.
item.extractor_note: This is the clearest minimal pair in the section — same content, one variable (grouping) changed, both results shown with their derived structures. The caption states the claim, so a text-only extraction keeps the claim and loses the proof.

item.question: What does this source say changed after economic liberalisation, and why is this the object in the record most likely to be out of date?
item.answer: She describes a double movement: 'one set of processes creates identifiable symbols of cultural identity while another lays down the universal ground within which these markers of difference operate.' The mechanism she names in the trade is concrete — 'advertising agencies in India — the new Ravi Varmas, if you will — often use proprietary analytical models from their parent companies overseas, filling in the blanks with content specific to Indian market segments.' With it comes a narrowing of what 'culture' is taken to mean: circumscribed, globally portable signs of heterogeneity — language, dress, food, music, art, rituals, festivals — grafted onto the protocols of a putatively universal modernity, which relegates cultural difference to leisure and harnesses it to niche marketing. IT IS THE MOST DATED OBJECT IN THE RECORD because it is a characterisation of a media landscape observed to roughly 2004-06, drawn largely from one firm's transformation seen at two points, and it precedes the Indian smartphone, cheap mobile data, UPI and streaming entirely — any of which would change the picture materially.
item.support: agencies 'use proprietary analytical models from their parent companies overseas, filling in the blanks with content specific to Indian market segments'
item.confounders: The template-plus-local-content observation is sharp and quotable, which is precisely why its date and its narrow evidence base need to travel with it.

source_terms: Spatial zones are areas within a page or spread that are designated for specific functions, or assigned particular kinds of content, as a means of both invigorating layouts and helping readers navigate.
spatial zones add some of the qualities of a hierarchic grid into grids defined by regular intervals
item.claim: Spatial zones are regions of a page or spread designated for a function or a kind of content, both to invigorate layouts and to help readers navigate. In a column grid a flowline or two defines horizontal zones and a column or group of columns defines vertical ones; in a modular grid groups of rows or columns do the same. A designer may also add a flowline or vertical guide independent of the grid's basic structure, deliberately interrupting its regularity to emphasise the zone; and modules may be grouped in mosaic-like patterns to make stepped or irregularly shaped zones. In effect, spatial zones add some of the qualities of a hierarchic grid to a grid defined by regular intervals — useful for separating continuous text from recurring sidebars or information graphics, or for correlating the text of a step-based process with the images illustrating each step.

mechanism.text: A zone is not a new kind of part; it is a role assigned to a group of existing parts, which is why it can be added to any regular structure without changing it.

scope.conditions: content with distinguishable functions inside one format

caveats.text: the source licenses adding a guide independent of the grid in order to emphasise a zone, which is a sanctioned violation appearing well before the section that discusses violation

positive.description: a website with three horizontal bands and vertical sub-zones in the lower two, separating navigation from content
a printmaking book dividing the spread with a single flowline: step text below, images above, images occasionally crossing the boundary

intra_source_relations.note: flowlines are how horizontal zones are made
brings hierarchic behaviour to a regular grid

provenance.section: Grid Basics — Subdividing Space: Spatial Zones

source_terms: any light positioned within the family of angles will produce a direct reflection
any light positioned outside of the family of angles will not light a mirror-like subject at all, at least as far as the camera can see
item.claim: Whether a direct reflection appears is decided entirely by whether the light sits inside the family of angles. A light inside it produces one; a light outside it does not light a mirror-like subject at all as far as the camera is concerned. To see direct reflection across most of a mirror-like surface, the source must be large enough to fill the family; to see none, both camera and light must be placed so the source falls outside it.

caveats.text: the source states it will use this principle repeatedly in later chapters, marking it as the chapter's operative result
the placement rule is a two-sided control — it says how to obtain the reflection and how to eliminate it — which is unusual among the craft rules seen in this batch

source_stated_remedies: use a light large enough to fill the family of angles to produce direct reflection across the surface
place both camera and light so the source falls outside the family of angles to eliminate direct reflection

positive.description: diagram of two lights, one inside the family producing a direct reflection and one outside producing none — described but not seen

intra_source_relations.note: the operative rule derived from the family

item.definition_in_origin_frame: The set of angles, taken over all points of a surface, at which a light source will produce a direct reflection visible from a given camera position. The source restricts the phrase to direct reflection, calling a diffuse equivalent meaningless.

source_terms: Direct reflections are a mirror image of the light source that produces them.
the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflectance
item.claim: A direct reflection is a mirror image of the light source. Light rays bounce from a smooth surface at the same angle at which they strike it, so the point from which a direct reflection can be seen is exactly determined by the angles between source, subject and camera.

mechanism.text: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflectance, which fixes the single viewing position from which the reflection is visible.

scope.conditions: smooth surfaces such as polished metal, water or glass

caveats.text: the source states no real subject produces a perfect direct reflection, though brightly polished metal, water or glass may nearly do so
